paper_metadata.title: Dynamic phase transition and dynamic recrystallization of Ti-B25 high-strength titanium alloy during high-temperature deformation

evidence.quote: The hot deformation behavior of Ti-B25 high-strength titanium alloy, primarily used in naval antenna tubes, was systematically investigated through stress-strain analysis and microstructure characterization using Electron Backscatter Diffraction (EBSD).

The DRX evolution process in the β phase of Ti-B25 alloy is analyzed by further observing the structure after hot compression at 1000 ◦ C, 0.01 s 1 with different deformation degrees (20 %, 40 %, and 60 %).

Fig. 2 shows the initial structure of Ti-B25 alloy, the microstructure contains both α and β phases. The α phase is more and most of the α grains are in the form of fine equiaxed or short rods. Furthermore, the average grain size of the initial microstructure is about 3.14 μ m.
The hot deformation behavior in the α + β phase region is the DPT of α phase, which is the main reason for the rapid decrease of the flow stress after reaching the peak value.

The most commonly accepted reason for this phenomenon is the dynamic strain aging effect triggered by the interaction of movable dislocations and solute atoms.

The cumulative orientation difference (point-to-point orientation difference) from point A to point B in Fig. 13 (c) above and the point-to-point orientation difference as shown in Fig. 13 (e) support the occurrence of CDRX, and similar phenomena are found in Ti-6554 alloy [55].

Characteristics of DDRX are also observed in the structure after hot compression. Some DRX grains often appear at the triple junctions of the uncrystallized grains, the content of LAGBs inside the uncrystallized grains is relatively low, and the grain boundaries tend to be jagged and expanded [56].
